questions.question: Harshvardhan's ambitions of extending his power to Deccan and South India were stopped by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulakesin II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pulakesin II was a renowned Chalukya king who ruled over the Deccan region.
 
• Harshavardhana, the ruler of North India, attempted to expand his influence to the Deccan and South India.
 
• Pulakesin II decisively defeated Harshavardhana near the banks of the river Narmada around 618-619 AD, halting his southern expansion.
 
• This victory is recorded in the Aihole inscription, composed by Pulakesin II's court poet, Ravikirti.
 
• The defeat of Harshavardhana by Pulakesin II is considered a significant event in Indian history as it marked the limit of Harshavardhana's territorial expansion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harshavardhana**

 
 
• Harshavardhana, also known as Harsha, was an Indian emperor who ruled North India from 606 to 647 AD.
 
• He established his capital at Kannauj and was known for his patronage of arts and literature.
 
• Harsha's reign is well-documented by the Chinese traveler Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang).
 
 
 
• **Chalukya Dynasty**
 
 
• The Chalukya dynasty was an important South Indian dynasty that ruled large parts of southern and central India between the 6th and 12th centuries.
 
• Pulakesin II was one of the most notable rulers of the Chalukya dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Aihole Inscription**
 
 
• The Aihole inscription is a famous historical record composed by Ravikirti, the court poet of Pulakesin II.
 
• It documents the achievements of Pulakesin II, including his victory over Harshavardhana.
 
 
 
• **Narmada River**
 
 
• The Narmada River is one of the major rivers in central India, flowing westwards over a length of about 1,312 km.
 
• The battle between Harshavardhana and Pulakesin II took place near this river.

questions.question: When was India's first ever budget presented?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1860**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **James Wilson**, a Scottish economist and politician, presented India's first budget on **18 February 1860**.
 
• He was the founder of The Economist magazine and also served as the Finance Member in the Council of the Governor-General of India.
 
• The budget was presented during the tenure of Lord Canning, the then Governor-General of India.
 
• This budget laid the groundwork for financial governance and economic management in British India.
 
• James Wilson's budget was aimed at addressing the financial challenges post the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Rebellion of 1857**

 
 
• Also known as the First War of Indian Independence, it was a major, but ultimately unsuccessful, uprising against the British East India Company.
 
• The rebellion led to significant changes in British policies and governance in India.
 
• After the rebellion, the British Crown took direct control of India from the East India Company.
 
 
 
• **Lord Canning**
 
 
• He was the Governor-General of India during the Indian Rebellion of 1857 and the first Viceroy of India.
 
• He played a crucial role in the reorganization of the Indian administration post-rebellion.
 
 
 
• **James Wilson's Contributions**
 
 
• Besides presenting India's first budget, he established the paper currency system in India.
 
• He introduced several financial and tax reforms that had long-lasting impacts on the Indian economy.
 
 
 
• **Economic Reforms Post-1857**
 
 
• The British government introduced various reforms to stabilize the economy and administration of India post-rebellion.
 
• These included the introduction of income tax and the establishment of a structured financial administration.

questions.question: The cytoplasmic zone surrounding the Golgi complex possesses no cell organelles. This zone of clear cytoplasm is called
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**zone of exclusion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The zone of exclusion is a cytoplasmic region surrounding the Golgi apparatus where no other organelles are present.
 
• This clear zone helps in the efficient functioning of the Golgi complex by providing an unobstructed area for vesicle formation and transport.
 
• The Golgi complex is a critical organelle involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or use within the cell.
 
• The zone of exclusion ensures that the Golgi complex remains free from interference by other cellular structures, facilitating its role in cellular logistics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Golgi Apparatus**

 
 
• Also known as the Golgi complex or Golgi body, it is an essential cell organelle found in most eukaryotic cells.
 
• It was discovered by the Italian scientist Camillo Golgi in 1898.
 
• The main function of the Golgi apparatus is to process and package macromolecules like proteins and lipids that are synthesized by the cell.
 
• It is composed of flattened membranous sacs known as cisternae.
 
 
 
• **Vesicle Transport**
 
 
• Vesicles are small structures within the cell that transport substances between organelles and to the cell membrane for secretion.
 
• The formation and transport of vesicles are crucial for the functioning of the Golgi apparatus.
 
• Vesicle-mediated transport ensures that proteins and lipids reach their correct destinations within or outside the cell.
 
 
 
• **Cytoplasm**
 
 
• The cytoplasm is the gel-like substance enclosed within the cell membrane and outside the nuclear membrane.
 
• It contains all organelles and cell parts, providing a medium for chemical reactions to occur.
 
• The cytoplasm plays a role in maintaining cell shape and consistency, and in storing nutrients and waste products.
 
 
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**
 
 
• The ER is a network of membranous tubules within the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells.
 
• It comes in two forms: rough ER (with ribosomes on its surface) and smooth ER (without ribosomes).
 
• The rough ER is involved in protein synthesis and quality control, while the smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct in context of Buddhist architecture?

i. Uddeshika stupa was created as a memorial.

ii. Paribhogika stupa contained the buried bodily remains of Buddha.

iii. Bharhut stupa is situated in Uttar Pradesh.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only i and ii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Uddeshika stupa** was created as a memorial, often constructed to commemorate significant events or places associated with Buddha's life.
 
• **Paribhogika stupa** contained the buried bodily remains (relics) of Buddha or other important monks, serving as a relic shrine.
 
• Bharhut stupa is not situated in Uttar Pradesh; it is located in **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• Bharhut stupa is renowned for its intricate railings and gateways adorned with detailed carvings depicting Jataka tales.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanchi Stupa:** Located in Madhya Pradesh, it is one of the oldest stone structures in India and a significant monument of Buddhist architecture.
 
• **Amaravati Stupa:** Situated in Andhra Pradesh, this stupa is known for its rich and elaborate carvings depicting scenes from the life of the Buddha.
 
• **Great Stupa at Sanchi:** Originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, it has a large hemispherical dome and houses relics of the Buddha.
 
• **Stupa Components:** Key elements include the dome (anda), the square railing (harmika) atop the dome, and the central pillar (yasti) symbolizing the axis mundi.
 
• **Function of Stupas:** Stupas functioned as places of meditation, pilgrimage, and veneration, reflecting the spread and influence of Buddhism.

questions.question: If an Indian citizen is denied entry to a public place because of his caste, which of the following Fundamental Rights is denied to him?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to equality**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Right to Equality is enshrined in Articles 14 to 18 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It guarantees that every citizen shall be treated equally before the law and prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• Denial of entry to a public place based on caste is a direct violation of Article 15(2), which prohibits discrimination on such grounds in public places.
 
• This fundamental right ensures that all citizens have equal access to public places like shops, restaurants, hotels, and places of public entertainment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 14:** Ensures equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• **Article 15:** Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• **Article 16:** Guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
 
• **Article 17:** Abolishes "untouchability" and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• **Article 18:** Abolishes titles except military and academic distinctions.

questions.question: 'Ram Navami' is celebrated in India to commemorate the:

options.text: coronation ceremony of Lord Rama as a king.
return of Lord Rama from forest.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**birth of Lord Rama**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ram Navami** is a Hindu festival that celebrates the birth of Lord Rama, the seventh avatar of the god Vishnu.
 
• It falls on the ninth day of the Hindu lunar calendar month of Chaitra, which typically occurs in March or April.
 
• Lord Rama is believed to have been born at noon, and this time is marked by special prayers and rituals.
 
• The festival is celebrated with various activities including fasting, singing devotional songs, reading the Ramayana, and visiting temples.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Significance of Ram Navami**

 
 
• Ram Navami marks the descent of Vishnu as Lord Rama, who is considered a symbol of virtue and chivalry.
 
• Lord Rama's story is chronicled in the ancient Indian epic, the Ramayana, which is revered by Hindus worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Celebration Practices**
 
 
• Devotees clean and decorate their homes, perform puja (worship), and recite verses from the Ramayana.
 
• Many people observe a day-long fast, breaking it only after performing evening prayers.
 
 
 
• **Temples and Public Celebrations**
 
 
• In Ayodhya, the birthplace of Lord Rama, grand celebrations are held with processions, and the city is illuminated with lights.
 
• Temples dedicated to Lord Rama organize special events, including recitations of the Ramayana and theatrical performances of his life story.
 
 
 
• **Symbolic Importance**
 
 
• Lord Rama's life and deeds exemplify righteousness, moral values, and the importance of fulfilling one's duties.
 
• Ram Navami serves as a reminder of these virtues, inspiring devotees to embody these qualities in their lives.

questions.question: In February 2024, who took an oath as the 12th Chief Minister of Jharkhand?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Champai Soren**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Champai Soren** was sworn in as the 12th Chief Minister of Jharkhand in February 2024.
 
• He is a member of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) party.
 
• Soren has previously held various ministerial positions in the Jharkhand state government.
 
• His political career is known for focusing on the rights and welfare of the tribal communities in Jharkhand.
 
• Soren succeeded Hemant Soren, who was the 11th Chief Minister of Jharkhand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM)**

 
 
• It is a state political party in Jharkhand founded by Shibu Soren.
 
• The party primarily focuses on the issues of tribal rights and regional development.
 
• JMM has been influential in Jharkhand politics since the state's formation in 2000.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Welfare in Jharkhand**
 
 
• Jharkhand has a significant tribal population, comprising around 26% of the state's total population.
 
• Various state and central government schemes aim to improve the socio-economic status of the tribal communities.
 
• Key initiatives include educational scholarships, health programs, and land rights legislation.
 
 
 
• **Political Landscape of Jharkhand**
 
 
• Jharkhand has a multi-party system with major parties including JMM, BJP, and Congress.
 
• Political dynamics in the state often revolve around issues like tribal rights, resource management, and industrial development.
 
• The state has witnessed frequent changes in leadership and coalition governments.
 
 
 
• **Hemant Soren**
 
 
• He served as the 11th Chief Minister of Jharkhand.
 
• He is also a member of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM).
 
• His tenure focused on tribal welfare, development projects, and combating corruption.

questions.question: Udit Narayan was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2016 for which of the following fields?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Art - Playback Singing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Udit Narayan is a renowned playback singer in the Indian film industry, predominantly known for his work in Bollywood.
 
• He has lent his voice to numerous hit songs in various Indian languages, making him a celebrated figure in the music industry.
 
• In recognition of his significant contributions to the field of playback singing, he was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2016.
 
• The Padma Bhushan is the third-highest civilian award in India, conferred to individuals for distinguished service of a high order in any field.
 
• Udit Narayan's melodious voice has earned him multiple awards and accolades throughout his career, including several Filmfare Awards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Awards**

 
 
• The Padma Awards include Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.
 
• These awards are announced annually on Republic Day and are among the highest civilian honors in India.
 
• Padma Vibhushan is awarded for exceptional and distinguished service, Padma Bhushan for distinguished service of a high order, and Padma Shri for distinguished service in any field.
 
 
 
• **Playback Singing**
 
 
• Playback singing is a recording technique in which singers pre-record songs for movies, and actors lip-sync to the songs on screen.
 
• This practice is highly prevalent in the Indian film industry, particularly in Bollywood.
 
• Some of the most famous playback singers in India include Lata Mangeshkar, Kishore Kumar, and Asha Bhosle.
 
 
 
• **Udit Narayan's Career**
 
 
• Udit Narayan began his career in the early 1980s and quickly rose to fame with his versatile singing style.
 
• He has sung in numerous languages, including Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Bengali.
 
• Some of his most popular songs include "Pehla Nasha," "Tip Tip Barsa Pani," and "Papa Kehte Hain."
 
 
 
• **Filmfare Awards**
 
 
• The Filmfare Awards are one of the oldest and most prestigious film awards in India, presented annually by The Times Group.
 
• They recognize artistic and technical excellence in the Hindi film industry.
 
• Udit Narayan has won several Filmfare Awards for Best Male Playback Singer throughout his career.

questions.question: Which river is known as 'Langchen Khambab' in Tibet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sutlej**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sutlej River is known as **'Langchen Khambab'** in Tibet.
 
• It is the longest of the five rivers that flow through the historic region of Punjab in northern India and Pakistan.
 
• The Sutlej originates from Lake Rakshastal in Tibet near Mount Kailash.
 
• It flows through India and Pakistan, eventually merging with the Chenab River in Pakistan.
 
• The Sutlej plays a vital role in the Indus Basin irrigation system, which is crucial for agriculture in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Importance**

 
 
• The Sutlej is an essential part of the Indus River system, contributing significantly to the region's water resources.
 
• It supports extensive irrigation systems that are critical for the agriculture of Punjab in both India and Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Hydropower Projects**
 
 
• The Sutlej River hosts several hydropower projects, such as the Bhakra-Nangal Dam, which is one of the largest dams in India.
 
• These projects are vital for generating electricity and providing water for irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• The river has been historically significant, with several ancient civilizations and cities flourishing along its banks.
 
• It has been a crucial route for trade and cultural exchange between India and Tibet.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns**
 
 
• Like many rivers, the Sutlej faces environmental challenges such as pollution, over-extraction of water, and impacts of climate change.
 
• Efforts are being made to address these issues through sustainable management practices.

questions.question: Bal Gangadhar described _____ as a diamond of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak, a prominent Indian nationalist leader, described Gopal Krishna Gokhale as the "diamond of India".
 
• Gokhale was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and a social reformer during the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was known for his moderate views and advocacy of dialogue and reform over confrontation with the British government.
 
• Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905, which worked for the expansion of education and social welfare in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**

 
 
• Founded in 1885, the INC was a major political party in India that led the country to independence.
 
• It played a crucial role in the Indian freedom struggle against British rule.
 
 
 
• **Servants of India Society**
 
 
• Founded by Gokhale in 1905, it aimed to promote education, sanitation, healthcare, and fight against social evils.
 
• The society was instrumental in mobilizing public opinion for social reforms.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**
 
 
• Known as "Lokmanya", Tilak was a fiery independence activist and a contemporary of Gokhale.
 
• He was a proponent of self-rule and used the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it".
 
 
 
• **Moderates and Extremists**
 
 
• In the early 20th century, the INC was divided into two factions: the Moderates led by Gokhale, and the Extremists led by Tilak.
 
• Moderates advocated for gradual reforms, while Extremists favored more direct action against British rule.

questions.question: 'The Blue Umbrella', 'The Cherry Tree', 'The Hidden Pool' are novels written by who among the following authors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ruskin Bond**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ruskin Bond** is a celebrated Indian author of British descent.
 
• He has written numerous novels, short stories, and children's books.
 
• Notable works include 'The Blue Umbrella', 'The Cherry Tree', and 'The Hidden Pool'.
 
• His works are characterized by their simplicity and the depiction of nature and rural life in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ruskin Bond's Literary Contributions**

 
 
• He has written over 500 short stories, essays, and novels.
 
• His first novel, 'The Room on the Roof', won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize in 1957.
 
• He was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1992 for his short story collection 'Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra'.
 
• He received the Padma Shri in 1999 and the Padma Bhushan in 2014.
 
 
 
• **The Blue Umbrella**
 
 
• This novella was published in 1980 and is one of Bond's most famous works.
 
• It tells the story of a young girl named Binya and her blue umbrella, exploring themes of kindness and material desire.
 
• The book was adapted into a film directed by Vishal Bhardwaj in 2005.
 
 
 
• **The Cherry Tree**
 
 
• A children's book that illustrates the importance of nature and nurturing.
 
• It follows the story of a young boy named Rakesh who plants a cherry seed and watches it grow.
 
 
 
• **The Hidden Pool**
 
 
• Published in 1966, it is Bond's first novel for children.
 
• The story revolves around three friends and their adventures around a hidden pool in the hills of Mussoorie.

questions.question: What is the overarching programme introduced in the Union Budget, 2018-19 by Government of India, for the school education sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samagra Shiksha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Samagra Shiksha** is an integrated scheme for school education extending from pre-school to class XII.
 
• It was launched by the Government of India in the Union Budget 2018-19.
 
• The scheme subsumes three earlier schemes: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA), and Teacher Education (TE).
 
• Samagra Shiksha aims to improve school effectiveness in terms of equal opportunities for schooling and equitable learning outcomes.
 
• It focuses on the holistic development of children, enhancing the quality of education at all levels of schooling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Education (RTE)**

 
 
• Enshrined in Article 21A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Makes education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• Mandates free and compulsory education for this age group.
 
• Aims to improve literacy rates and ensure access to education for all children.
 
 
 
• **Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA)**
 
 
• Launched in 2009 to enhance access to secondary education.
 
• Aimed at improving the quality of education at the secondary level.
 
• Focused on reducing the drop-out rate and enhancing the enrolment ratio.
 
• Now subsumed under the Samagra Shiksha scheme.
 
 
 
• **Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA)**
 
 
• Launched in 2001 to achieve universalization of elementary education.
 
• Focused on providing useful and relevant elementary education for all children.
 
• Aimed at bridging social, regional, and gender gaps in education.
 
• Now part of the Samagra Shiksha initiative.
 
 
 
• **Teacher Education (TE)**
 
 
• Aims to improve the quality of teachers through professional development.
 
• Focuses on training and re-training teachers to enhance their teaching skills.
 
• Supports continuous professional development programs for teachers.
 
• Also integrated into the Samagra Shiksha scheme.

questions.question: Who was the highest run scorer in Men's World Cup cricket - 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rohit Sharma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rohit Sharma** was the highest run-scorer in the 2019 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup.
 
• He scored a total of **648 runs** in the tournament.
 
• Rohit Sharma achieved this feat by scoring **five centuries** in the tournament, a record in World Cup history.
 
• His batting average in the 2019 World Cup was **81.00**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2019**

 
 
• The 2019 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup was held in England and Wales from May 30 to July 14, 2019.
 
• The tournament featured ten teams competing in a round-robin format followed by semi-finals and a final.
 
• England won the tournament, defeating New Zealand in the final via boundary count after a Super Over tie.
 
 
 
• **Rohit Sharma's World Cup Performance**
 
 
• Rohit Sharma became the first player to score five centuries in a single World Cup tournament.
 
• His centuries came against South Africa, Pakistan, England, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka.
 
 
 
• **Other Top Performers**
 
 
• David Warner of Australia was the second-highest run-scorer with 647 runs.
 
• Shakib Al Hasan of Bangladesh had an outstanding tournament, scoring 606 runs and taking 11 wickets.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• Prior to Rohit Sharma's record, the highest number of centuries in a single World Cup was four, achieved by Kumar Sangakkara in 2015.
 
• Sachin Tendulkar held the previous record for the most runs in a single World Cup, scoring 673 runs in the 2003 tournament.

questions.question: The approximate number of water molecules present in 9 gm of water is _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.011 × 10²³**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The molecular weight of water (H₂O) is approximately 18 grams per mole.
 
• 1 mole of any substance contains Avogadro's number of molecules, which is 6.022 × 10²³ molecules.
 
• 9 grams of water is equal to 0.5 moles of water (9 grams / 18 grams per mole).
 
• The number of water molecules in 0.5 moles is 0.5 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 3.011 × 10²³ molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mole Concept**

 
 
• The mole is a fundamental unit in chemistry representing the amount of a substance.
 
• 1 mole of any substance contains exactly 6.022 × 10²³ entities (atoms, molecules, ions, etc.)—a number known as Avogadro's number.
 
• The mole allows chemists to count and use substances in a practical and consistent manner.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Number**
 
 
• Avogadro's number is 6.022 × 10²³, which is the number of atoms, ions, or molecules in one mole of a substance.
 
• This constant is named after the Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro, who contributed to the understanding of molecular theory.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Weight**
 
 
• The molecular weight (or molar mass) of a substance is the mass of one mole of that substance, usually expressed in grams per mole (g/mol).
 
• For water (H₂O), the molecular weight is approximately 18 g/mol (2 g/mol for hydrogen atoms + 16 g/mol for an oxygen atom).
 
 
 
• **Calculating Moles**
 
 
• The number of moles of a substance can be calculated by dividing the mass of the substance by its molecular weight.
 
• For example, 9 grams of water divided by its molecular weight (18 g/mol) results in 0.5 moles of water.

questions.concept: Foundation of the Indian National Congress

questions.question: Who among the following was defeated by Babur in the Battle of Khanwa in 1527 CE?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rana Sanga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Battle of Khanwa was fought on 16 March 1527.
 
• It was a decisive victory for Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• Rana Sanga was the ruler of Mewar and led a Rajput confederacy against Babur.
 
• This battle consolidated Babur's control over northern India and marked the end of significant Rajput resistance.
 
• Babur employed modern tactics such as the use of field artillery which played a crucial role in his victory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Babur:**

 
 
• He was the founder of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• Babur was a descendant of Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's side.
 
• He introduced the use of gunpowder and artillery in Indian warfare.
 
• His memoirs, known as the Baburnama, provide a detailed account of his life and conquests.
 
 
 
• **Rana Sanga:**
 
 
• He was a prominent Rajput ruler of Mewar.
 
• Rana Sanga is known for his bravery and military prowess.
 
• He aimed to re-establish Rajput dominance in northern India.
 
• Despite his defeat, he is remembered as a hero in Rajput history.
 
 
 
• **Field Artillery in the Battle:**
 
 
• The use of field artillery by Babur was revolutionary in Indian warfare.
 
• It provided a significant advantage against the traditional cavalry-based armies of Indian rulers.
 
• The effective use of cannons and gunpowder helped Babur secure decisive victories.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Battle:**
 
 
• The Battle of Khanwa established Mughal supremacy in northern India.
 
• It marked the decline of the Rajput power in the region.
 
• This victory paved the way for the expansion of the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: Where was the inaugural match of the first edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL) organised in the year 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The inaugural match of the first edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL) was held in **Mumbai** in 2023.
 
• The venue chosen for this historic match was the **Dr. DY Patil Sports Academy** in Navi Mumbai.
 
• The Women's Premier League is organized by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (**BCCI**).
 
• The WPL aims to provide a platform for female cricketers to showcase their talent on a larger stage.
 
• This league is expected to significantly boost women's cricket in India and worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Women's Premier League (WPL)**

 
 
• The WPL is a professional women's Twenty20 cricket league in India.
 
• It was officially announced by the BCCI in 2022 as a major step towards promoting women's cricket.
 
• The league features teams representing different cities and regions of India.
 
• The WPL follows the format and structure similar to the Indian Premier League (IPL).
 
 
 
• **Dr. DY Patil Sports Academy**
 
 
• Located in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, it is a premier sports complex known for hosting various cricket matches.
 
• It has a seating capacity of approximately 55,000 spectators.
 
• Besides cricket, the stadium is also used for football and other sporting events.
 
 
 
• **Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI)**
 
 
• The BCCI is the national governing body for cricket in India.
 
• Founded in December 1928, it is responsible for organizing domestic and international cricket matches in India.
 
• The BCCI also oversees the development of cricket infrastructure and talent at the grassroots level.
 
 
 
• **Impact of WPL on Women's Cricket**
 
 
• The WPL provides female cricketers with greater visibility and opportunities for professional growth.
 
• It helps in bridging the gap between men's and women's cricket in terms of popularity and investment.
 
• The league is expected to inspire young girls to take up cricket as a career.

questions.question: 'Chakyar Koothu', the folk dance form in which the entire story is presented by a single performer, primarily belongs to which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chakyar Koothu** is a traditional performing art form from Kerala.
 
• It is a solo performance where the performer narrates stories from Hindu epics, especially the **Mahabharata and Ramayana**.
 
• The performer uses a combination of **expressive facial gestures, hand movements, and vocal recitations** to convey the story.
 
• **Mani Madhava Chakyar** is one of the most famous exponents of Chakyar Koothu.
 
• The performance is traditionally done in temples and is considered a part of the **Koodiyattam** genre.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Koodiyattam:**

 
 
• An ancient form of Sanskrit theatre performed in Kerala.
 
• Recognized by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.
 
 
 
• **Natyashastra:**
 
 
• An ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts, encompassing theatre, dance, and music.
 
• Attributed to the sage Bharata Muni.
 
 
 
• **Mani Madhava Chakyar:**
 
 
• A legendary performer known for popularizing Chakyar Koothu and Koodiyattam.
 
• Honored with prestigious awards such as Padma Shri and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.
 
 
 
• **Temple Theatre:**
 
 
• Traditional venues in Kerala where classical art forms like Chakyar Koothu are performed.
 
• These performances are often part of temple festivals and rituals.

questions.question: Which of the following sectors had the largest percentage of workforce in urban India in the year 2019-2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Service**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The service sector dominated the urban workforce in India in 2019-2020.
 
• Approximately 60% of the urban workforce was employed in the service sector during this period.
 
• The service sector includes industries like IT, retail, hospitality, healthcare, and education.
 
• This sector's growth is attributed to the rapid urbanization and increased demand for professional services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urbanization in India**

 
 
• Urbanization refers to the increasing population in urban areas compared to rural areas.
 
• India has seen a steady increase in urbanization, with urban population growing from 27.81% in 2001 to 34.93% in 2020.
 
• Economic opportunities, better living standards, and improved infrastructure are key drivers of urbanization.
 
 
 
• **Growth of the IT Sector**
 
 
• The IT sector has been a significant contributor to the service industry in urban India.
 
• India is a global leader in IT services, outsourcing, and software development.
 
• This sector provides employment to millions of professionals in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Employment Distribution**
 
 
• Employment in urban areas is mainly concentrated in the service sector, followed by industry and agriculture.
 
• Industries such as manufacturing, construction, and mining also play a role, but to a lesser extent.
 
 
 
• **Economic Contribution**
 
 
• The service sector is the largest contributor to India's GDP, accounting for around 54% as of 2020.
 
• This sector's significant contribution highlights its importance in the overall economic landscape of the country.

questions.question: National Prophylaxis Program, which was launched in 1970 as an immediate remedial measure to address which of the following medical conditions/diseases caused by nutritional deficiencies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Blindness. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The National Prophylaxis Programme against Nutritional Blindness was launched in 1970 by the Government of India to tackle nutritional blindness caused by Vitamin A deficiency.
 
• It mainly focused on children below 5 years of age, who are most vulnerable to Vitamin A deficiency.
 
• Severe deficiency of Vitamin A can lead to xerophthalmia (dry eyes), night blindness, and ultimately, complete blindness.
 
• The program involved distribution of Vitamin A supplements (200,000 IU doses every 6 months) to prevent and treat deficiency.
 
• Over the years, the program significantly helped reduce cases of nutritional blindness among children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hypercalcemia**

 
 
• **Definition**: A condition caused by high levels of calcium in the blood.
 
• Not related to deficiency but rather an excess (often due to overuse of supplements, hyperparathyroidism, or cancer).
 
• **Keyword**: "Hyper" means excessive, "calcemia" means calcium in blood.
 
 
 
• **Goitre**
 
 
• **Cause**: Caused by iodine deficiency, not Vitamin A.
 
• **Related Program**: Addressed under the National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme (NIDDCP).
 
• **Keyword**: Enlargement of the thyroid gland due to lack of iodine in diet.
 
 
 
• **Beriberi**
 
 
• **Cause**: Caused by Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) deficiency.
 
• **Types**: Two types – dry beriberi (affecting nerves) and wet beriberi (affecting cardiovascular system).
 
• Unrelated to Vitamin A or the blindness program.
 
 
 
• **Key Takeaways / Keywords:**
 
 
• Vitamin A Deficiency → Nutritional Blindness
 
• Vitamin B1 Deficiency → Beriberi
 
• Iodine Deficiency → Goitre
 
• Hypercalcemia → Excess Calcium (Not a deficiency disorder)

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution directs the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 163**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 163 of the Indian Constitution mandates that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Governor.
 
• The Governor is generally required to act on the advice of the Council of Ministers, except in cases where the Constitution specifies that he can act in his discretion.
 
• The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state.
 
• This Article ensures a parliamentary system of government in the states, similar to the system followed at the Union level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 154**

 
 
• It states that the executive power of the state is vested in the Governor and is exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him.
 
 
 
• **Article 164**
 
 
• This Article deals with the appointment of the Chief Minister and other ministers by the Governor.
 
• It specifies that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state.
 
 
 
• **Article 167**
 
 
• The Chief Minister is required to communicate to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of the state and proposals for legislation.
 
 
 
• **Article 153**
 
 
• It states that there shall be a Governor for each state, but one person can be appointed as Governor for two or more states.

questions.question: As per the reforms of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2023, how many minerals have been removed from the list of atomic minerals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

__
 
• The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2023 was introduced to reform the mining sector in India.
 
• A total of 6 minerals have been removed from the list of atomic minerals under this amendment.
 
• This amendment aims to stimulate private investment and boost the mining sector's growth.
 
• The removal of these minerals from the list will simplify the regulatory framework and promote ease of doing business.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atomic Minerals**

 
 
• These minerals are used for the generation of nuclear energy and other nuclear applications.
 
• Examples include uranium, thorium, and other rare earth elements.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the Amendment**
 
 
• To enhance the ease of doing business in the mining sector.
 
• To attract private investments and boost the sector's growth.
 
 
 
• **Impact on the Mining Sector**
 
 
• The amendment is expected to create more job opportunities.
 
• It aims to increase the contribution of the mining sector to the national GDP.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework**
 
 
• The reform intends to simplify the regulatory procedures for mining activities.
 
• It will enhance transparency and streamline the process of obtaining mining leases.

questions.question: K Kalyanasundaram Pillai was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, 1999, for his contribution to which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• K Kalyanasundaram Pillai was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1999 for his exemplary contribution to Bharatnatyam.
 
• Bharatnatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating from Tamil Nadu.
 
• Pillai hails from a distinguished family of Bharatnatyam dancers and is known for his exceptional choreography and teaching.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is one of the highest national recognitions given to practicing artists by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatnatyam**

 
 
• Bharatnatyam is characterized by precise footwork, intricate hand gestures, and expressive facial expressions.
 
• It is traditionally performed by solo dancers and is deeply connected to the music and literature of South India.
 
• The dance form is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and the combination of abstract dance sequences with expressive dance sequences.
 
• Key components of Bharatnatyam include Nritta (pure dance), Nritya (expressive dance), and Natya (dramatic storytelling).
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**
 
 
• Established in 1952, the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is given annually by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, the national academy for music, dance, and drama in India.
 
• The award is recognized as the highest honor in the field of performing arts in India.
 
• Awardees receive a citation, an angavastram (a traditional Indian shawl), and a cash prize.
 
• The award aims to recognize and honor the outstanding contribution of artists in the fields of music, dance, and drama.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dance Forms of India**
 
 
• **Kathak**: Originating from North India, it emphasizes rhythmic foot movements adorned with small bells and the expression of stories through dance.
 
• **Kuchipudi**: A dance-drama performance originating from Andhra Pradesh, known for its fast rhythms and fluid movements.
 
• **Odissi**: Originating from Odisha, it is known for its sculpturesque poses and fluid movements.
 
• **Manipuri**: Originating from the state of Manipur, it is characterized by smooth and graceful movements.

questions.question: A portion of landmass from the shore line up to the shelf break that is submerged under shallow water is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Continental Shelf**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **continental shelf** is the extended perimeter of each continent, which lies submerged under relatively shallow seas and gulfs.
 
• It extends from the **shoreline to the continental slope**, where the seafloor drops steeply.
 
• Continental shelves are typically **characterized by their relatively shallow waters**, generally less than 200 meters deep.
 
• These areas are often rich in **marine life and resources** such as oil and natural gas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Continental Slope**

 
 
• The continental slope marks the boundary between the continental shelf and the deep ocean basin.
 
• It is characterized by a steep incline and can drop from a depth of about 200 meters to over 3,000 meters.
 
 
 
• **Continental Rise**
 
 
• The continental rise is found between the continental slope and the abyssal plain.
 
• It consists of thick accumulations of sediments that have been transported down the continental slope.
 
 
 
• **Oceanic Basin**
 
 
• Oceanic basins are large depressions on the Earth's surface that contain the oceans.
 
• They are composed of the oceanic crust and are usually deeper than 2,000 meters.
 
 
 
• **Continental Drift**
 
 
• Continental drift is the movement of the Earth's continents relative to each other by appearing to drift across the ocean bed.
 
• This theory was proposed by Alfred Wegener in 1912.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in the three main dimensions of the New Industrial Policy, 1991, announced by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Urbanisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The New Industrial Policy of 1991 was formulated to **liberalize the Indian economy** and stimulate industrial growth.
 
• The three main dimensions of the New Industrial Policy are **Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation**.
 
• **Liberalisation** refers to the reduction of government regulations and restrictions in the economy to encourage private sector activity.
 
• **Privatisation** involves the transfer of ownership and management of public sector enterprises to the private sector.
 
• **Globalisation** focuses on integrating the Indian economy with the global economy through increased foreign trade and investment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liberalisation**

 
 
• Involves reducing tariffs, trade barriers, and regulatory restrictions to enhance economic efficiency.
 
• Aims to create a more competitive environment to foster innovation and growth.
 
 
 
• **Privatisation**
 
 
• Focuses on improving the efficiency and productivity of public enterprises.
 
• Encourages private investment and management in industries previously controlled by the government.
 
 
 
• **Globalisation**
 
 
• Encourages foreign direct investment (FDI) and international trade.
 
• Aims to integrate the Indian economy with the global market for better access to technology and capital.
 
 
 
• **New Industrial Policy of 1991**
 
 
• Announced by the Government of India to address the economic crisis of the early 1990s.
 
• Marked a significant shift from a mixed economy towards a more market-oriented economy.
